groups.title: Forest
groups.subtitle: Terrestrial and airborne laser scanning, 360° imagery and models of forest structure

subs.title: Canopy structure, light and ground truth — Q-ForestLab data
subs.text: Open TLS data from Q-ForestLab (Ghent University, CC BY 4.0): four plots from tropical rainforest to alpine conifer forest with every tree labelled, plus a large old tropical tree scanned from the ground and from the canopy. Colourings: height, ground truth, single trees, strata, light at the ground.

subs.title: One stand, the whole chain — Renon / ICOS IT-Ren
subs.text: Norway spruce stand in South Tyrol (Leica BLK360, E57): panorama, point cloud, single trees, DBH, QSM, growth projection, occlusion, synthetic scan and Gaussian splatting of the same site.

subs.title: Benchmarks with ground truth
subs.text: Point clouds with manual labels or field measurements: how well do detection, segmentation and DBH work?

subs.title: Hedgerows and agricultural landscape
subs.text: Hedges and tree rows from TLS and open ALS: structure index and habitat suitability.

subs.title: 360° forest panoramas
subs.text: Openly licensed forest panoramas as input to the panorama pipeline (consumer 360° cameras, HDRIs, a VR study).

subs.title: Photorealistic 3D — Gaussian splatting
subs.text: Walkable photorealistic models trained from photos (WASD/mouse).

subs.title: Historic buildings and sites in 3D — Gaussian splatting
subs.text: Photorealistic, walkable 3D models trained from open image sets; the Pellis buildings are checked against a photogrammetric reference point cloud.
